title: Childhood in Jefferson Parish and the grocery string band
summary: His mother died when he was 10; he worked for German grocers, entertained there, and joined a string band on bass violin taught by Professor Umphrey.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Thanks. My name is William Ridgely. I was born in Jefferson Parish, January 15, 18 and 82. My mother died when I was 10 and I had to go to work. And there was some German people that I knew that ran a country grocery about two city blocks from where I was born. And they gave me a job. And I worked for those people about 18 years. And after I was with them a while, it was a place where most of the men in the country gathered in the evening and sat around and talked. And a lot of young boys. And I used to do a lot of entertaining at night with those men by dancing and singing. Some of the boys played banjo. And we made up in our mind to set up what we call a string band. There were six of us. And I was in the points. And so my people that I worked for, they bought a bass violin for me. That was the first instrument that I started on. And there were six of us. We didn't have any trombone player at that time.
What were the instruments in that family?
There was bass violin, banjo, clarinet, cornet, and drums.
I see. And what were you playing?
I played bass violin. And Professor Umphrey, James Umphrey, was our instructor. And he lived in New Orleans. We lived in the parish.
Just about where was that in the Jefferson?
